subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Neuroendocrine neoplasms: grading, functional syndromes and targeted radionuclide therapy

steps.tx: Gastroenteropancreatic **neuroendocrine tumours** (NETs) are categorized by mitotic count and **Ki-67 proliferation** index. The World Health Organization system recognizes well-differentiated grade 1 tumours with Ki-67 under 3%, grade 2 tumours with Ki-67 between 3% to 20%, and grade 3 tumours with Ki-67 over 20%. These well-differentiated neoplasms remain biologically distinct from poorly differentiated **neuroendocrine carcinomas** which display diffuse severe atypia.

steps.tx: Malignant **carcinoid syndrome** occurs when circulating vasoactive humors bypass first-pass hepatic inactivation, predominantly following liver metastases. Systemic release of **serotonin**, histamine, kallikrein, and prostaglandins triggers episodic cutaneous flushing, secretory watery diarrhoea, and bronchospasm. Over time, high circulating serotonin levels induce fibrotic tricuspid regurgitation and pulmonary stenosis, causing debilitating right-sided carcinoid heart disease.
steps.say: Malignant carcinoid syndrome occurs when circulating vasoactive humors bypass first-pass hepatic inactivation, predominantly following liver metastases. Systemic release of serotonin, histamine, and prostaglandins triggers episodic cutaneous flushing, secretory watery diarrhoea, and bronchospasm. Chronic serotonin exposure causes debilitating right-sided carcinoid heart disease.

steps.tx: Biochemical confirmation of carcinoid syndrome relies on measuring breakdown products of endogenous monoamines. Quantitative urinary 24-hour **5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid** (**5-HIAA**) is the principal diagnostic test. Patients must maintain dietary serotonin restriction for at least 3 days prior to urine collection, avoiding bananas, walnuts, pineapples, and avocados to eliminate false-positive test elevations.

steps.tx: Molecular functional imaging exploiting cell-surface somatostatin receptors provides sensitive tumour staging. Positron emission tomography using gallium-68 **DOTATATE** or DOTATOC binds **somatostatin receptor** subtype 2 with high nanomolar affinity. Gallium-68 DOTATATE PET-CT displays superior detection sensitivity compared to conventional octreoscan or anatomical computed tomography, successfully identifying occult primary tumours and distant bony metastases.

Positron emission tomography using gallium-68 DOTATATE binds somatostatin receptor subtype 2 with high affinity. Gallium-68 DOTATATE PET-CT displays superior detection sensitivity compared to conventional octreoscan.

steps.tx: Synthetic **somatostatin analogues** provide dual therapeutic benefits by controlling hormone hypersecretion and arresting tumour growth. Depot formulations of **octreotide** LAR and **lanreotide** autogel demonstrated significant antiproliferative prolongation of progression-free survival in the landmark PROMID and CLARINET randomized trials. These subcutaneous or intramuscular analogues serve as first-line maintenance monotherapy for stable or slowly progressive gastrointestinal and pancreatic NETs.

steps.tx: **Peptide receptor radionuclide** therapy represents an established targeted approach for advanced somatostatin receptor-positive neoplasms. The phase 3 **NETTER-1** trial evaluated beta-emitting lutetium-177 dotatate in progressive midgut neuroendocrine tumours. Lutetium-177 dotatate achieved a marked 79% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death alongside significant overall survival benefit, establishing PRRT as standard second-line therapy.

steps.tx: Molecular pathways regulating cellular growth and metabolism provide alternative therapeutic targets in progressive neoplasms. **Everolimus** is an oral **mTOR inhibitor** approved for progressive, well-differentiated non-functional gastrointestinal and pulmonary NETs based on the RADIANT-4 trial. By blocking downstream mammalian target of rapamycin signalling, daily everolimus provides meaningful delay in tumour progression with manageable side effects including aphthous stomatitis and rash.

steps.tx: Poorly differentiated **neuroendocrine carcinoma** represents a distinct clinicopathological entity characterized by rapid progression and visceral crises. Tumour cells display marked pleomorphism, extensive necrosis, and a Ki-67 proliferation index exceeding 50%, driven by underlying TP53 and RB1 genomic alterations. Systemic treatment requires urgent frontline **platinum-etoposide** cytotoxic chemotherapy, mirroring regimens employed in small cell lung cancer.
